messages:
anya: quick heads-up — I hit a weird interaction between shard fallback, token-throttling, and preemption during a burst test.
anya: repro steps + short log below. seems like the allocator keeps moving the request to fallback shards, which then immediately preempt, causing a flurry of retries and throttle spikes.
anya: logs:
```
2026-02-14T15:02:01Z INFO admission: admit shard=shard-42 tenant=tn-17 tokens=256
2026-02-14T15:02:01Z WARN preempt: evicting lease shard=shard-42 reason=preemptible-credit-exhausted
2026-02-14T15:02:01Z INFO fallback: rerouting req=abc123 -> shard-7
2026-02-14T15:02:01Z WARN preempt: evicting lease shard=shard-7 reason=hotspot-preemption
2026-02-14T15:02:02Z ERROR admission: throttle spike tenant=tn-17 rate=450/s
```
anya: small harness to repro: `go test ./orchestrator -run TestShardFallbackPreempt`
sam: can you share the admission config that was used? quota, burst credits, and preemptible window?
anya: yep — default headroom 3, burst_credits=100, preemptible=true, eviction-priority: {burst: 5, preemptible: 10} (weirdly high).
julia: my hunch: fallback moves load to smaller-capacity shards without considering recent preempt history, so they get immediately evicted and re-fallback, which trips the global throttle.
mike: yeah — we saw similar in the old headroom experiments. solution space: (A) add per-shard cooldown after a preempt, (B) make fallback prefer shards with recent-stable flag, (C) delay fallback by a few 100ms to allow burst credits to refill.
anya: +1 on per-shard cooldown. simplest to reason about and low-risk.
sam: downside: might reduce availability for legitimate fallbacks (if cooldown too long). we need a metric to detect oscillation vs legit spill.
julia: propose a lightweight metric: `preempt_count_1m` + `reassigns_30s` and mark a shard as "flapping" when both exceed thresholds. Then admission treats flapping shards as last-resort.
mike: implementation note: we should keep the cooldown tied to the eviction type (preemptible vs hotspot). preemptible eviction -> short cooldown (seconds), hotspot/oom -> longer.
anya: do we want the allocator to signal the autoscaler to spin up capacity earlier in this case? i.e., if many fallbacks detected, bump scale intent.
sam: yes but cautious — we already have predictive intent. suggestion: emit a "fallback-amplification" metric and have the scaler's controller map that to a temporary scale intent with a low-confidence flag so operator can audit spikes.
julia: also think about admission surface: currently fallback is opaque to the caller. maybe add an optional hint in the request like `prefer_stable_shard=true` so heavy clients (batching encoder jobs) can avoid oscillation.
anya: good idea; that keeps path forward without changing default.
mike: for rollout, plan: implement per-shard flapping detector + cooldown in allocator (feature flag), emit fallback-amplification metric, and add request hint in SDK. roll out to canary for 48h.
anya: +1. I'll open a tiny RFC with the detector thresholds and a test harness.
sam: ping @orch-bot when you open the PR so CI can run the integration sim.
orch-bot: CI queued: orch-integration/sim-fallback 1723456801 -> status: queued :hourglass_flowing_sand:
anya: thanks — will do. status: drafting RFC and a short sim. will post link here when ready. :thumbsup:
